pages.text: Cold wind whooshes across the ice. Pip the penguin waddles forward, ready for a slippery adventure.
Pip is a bird, but he cannot fly. Instead, his wings work like flippers for swimming.
With a happy belly-flop, Pip slides down a smooth hill. Sliding saves energy on the ice.
At the edge, Pip dives into the sea. Penguins are strong swimmers, zooming after fish underwater.
Feathers keep Pip dry. Under his feathers, a layer of fat helps him stay warm in icy water.
Pip pops up to breathe air. Birds breathe air, even when they spend lots of time swimming.
Back on land, Pip meets his colony. Penguins gather in groups to stay safe and warm.
Some penguins take turns watching. Others rest. Working together helps the colony survive cold days.
The sun dips low. Pip remembers: slide on ice, swim like a torpedo, and stick with friends.
Night is quiet. Pip snuggles close to neighbors, warm and sleepy, while snow sparkles like tiny stars.
